newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tanzania inflation falls to 16.2 pct in October.
newsitem.headline: Tanzania inflation falls to 16.2 pct in October.

text.p: Tanzania's inflation rate fell to 16.2 percent in November from 18.8 percent in October, the central bank said in its latest monthly report.
The central Bank of Tanzania (BoT) attributed the fall to tight control of government spending and increased food supplies which kept prices low.
It said inflation should be lower at 15 percent in December 1996 and could reach 10 percent by the end of June 1997.

"Given the current tight anti-inflationary monetary and fiscal policy measures pursued by the Bank and the government respectively, as well as the satisfactory food supply situation, the inflation rate is expected to decline further," the report said.
The November rate represents an improvement of 5.6 points when compared with the 21.8 percent in December, 1995.
The government adopted a cash-budget system last fiscal year under which funds disbursed by the treasury each month are matched to revenue collected the previous month.
The bank says controlling Tanzania's inflation remains its highest priority.
